replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — this ruling is for both of you.

WHAT HAPPENED. The trace for TRP-00114 records 23.97 km driven against a booked optimal of 18.0 km: an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute). The excess does not reach either materiality gate (more than 50% of optimal, or more than 8.0 km), so this is an established but not a MATERIAL deviation, and the POL-RD-06 driver-profile consequences are not triggered. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing figure; the trip record's 24.0 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and was not used for the threshold. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 241 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s — so none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) fires and the deviation stands on the trace alone. (The admissibility pre-pass also left this artifact COMPLETE, so schema status and policy status agree here.)

THE DRIVER'S CONGESTION ACCOUNT. The driver's statement that the AYE was crawling and no advisory was known is an assertion that cites no evidence ID, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, carries no weight and is discarded. It also cannot discharge the driver's shifted burden, and it does not exonerate: POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) — no LTA advisory covers the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36–19:20 window. The driver's alternative escalation argument under POL-RD-10(5) is rejected: that limb fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is absent from the pool. Here no clause is invoked against any artifact — the congestion claim is a bare assertion citing nothing, and the driver's own primary position is that no POL-RD-03 exoneration is asserted. POL-RD-08's discard rule, not escalation, is what governs a bare excuse; otherwise every uncorroborated excuse would become an escalation. The absence of the advisory is citable, but the ruling does not rest on that artifact, so it does not touch the confidence floor.

NO OTHER EXONERATION. POL-RD-04 fails: the rider's message 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' is a challenge to the route, not an instruction, it carries no waypoint_hint and names no road the driver could act on. POL-RD-05 fails: no amendment timestamps and no amended optimal are stored, so there is nothing to re-run and POL-RD-05 cannot be applied (its own terms send a null re-quote to POL-RD-10(5), which is not the case here since no amendment is recorded at all). POL-RD-12 fails: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-11 fails: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance-and-time refund is not closed off.

THE MONEY. POL-RD-02 runs on the metered fare, with the surge multiplier taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 1.6 and applied to base, distance and time only, never to ERP.
  charged_total = 58.10
  recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 18.0 + 0.28 × 30.0) × 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 41.12 + 0.80 + 2.50 = 44.42
  refund = 58.10 − 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 13.70
That is 23.6% of the charge — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% FULL_REFUND line, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The driver is right that the recovery is capped by this arithmetic (13.70) and not by the 15.00 contested.

ERP (POL-RD-09). Of the 4.50 charged, the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and is properly chargeable and stays with the rider; the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off-route and is ALREADY comprehended in the 44.42 recomputed fare, because that fare includes only on-route gantries. It is itemised here for transparency and is not added on top of the 13.70 — adding it would double-count it. Neither line is a phantom: the trace passes within 250 m of both billed gantries, so POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity is not engaged and no referral arises.

BURDEN. The rider discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00114, started_at 18:40:00 matches the trace's first fix and ended_at 19:20:00 matches the last, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden then shifted to the driver and was not discharged with a specific artifact and clause.

OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70 to the rider; no driver compensation (billed distance 24.0 km exceeds the trace figure, so there is no unbilled shortfall to compensate); no conduct referral (no repeat-deviation pattern — deviation_flags_90d = 1 against completed_trips_90d = 412, neither the 3-flag nor the 0.05-ratio test) and no billing-integrity referral. Confidence is capped at 1.0 because every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — sits at weight_multiplier 1.0, and the uncorroborated counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and so is outside the cap. The driver's POL-RD-06 point is accepted: no pattern is established on the two permitted fields.
